cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a tray above the model like you. Welcome rain. Your cloud sent a drop upward; let's get it to the roof garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's catching a roof leak. One upward drop doesn't mean the model can water the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leaks caught, yes. It did go up. Mark that height on the ruler; we can test another inch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've folded the forecast over. It only predicts one inch, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the back for our notes. Raise the tray an inch and try another pulse; I'll count what reaches it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies an overhead tray as rain welcoming; A3 recovers from B2's leak explanation by proposing a measured trial, and A5 avoids confirming B4's adverse prediction while keeping B testing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 distinguishes a single upward drop from full garden supply; A3 proposes incremental height evidence, B4 questions its predicted limit, and A5 tests that exact increment.

relationship.evidence: B2 cares about whether the model can do its job; B4 wants the forecast, while A5 gives B another practical trial instead of an empty reassurance.

heightening.evidence: B4's one-inch prediction becomes A5's one-inch increase, and the folded forecast becomes note paper while its discouraging face stays hidden.

specificity.evidence: A3 now marks height on a ruler, not a horizontal tray impact; A5's raised tray is a measurable next test.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 requests a trial and volunteers to count, with no appended declaration of hope or explanation of the card.
